content.text:
I renamed the project from Floyd to Bastion. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes after the rename.

- **Remote:** `origin` now points at `tacoda_github:tacoda/bastion.git`.
- **Crates:** `floyd-ui` is now `bastion-ui`, `floyd` is now `bastion`, and `floyd_lib` is now `bastion_lib`. The `crates/floyd-spikes` directory is now `crates/bastion-spikes`, and `Cargo.lock` is updated to match.
- **Tauri:** the `productName` and window title are now `Bastion`, and the identifier is now `dev.tacoda.bastion`.
- **iii:** the namespace, the `bastion::…` function IDs, the `bastion-steps` queue, and `sqlite:./data/bastion.db` all use the new name.
- **Text:** `index.html`, `src/app.rs`, the capabilities file, and all doc comments now say Bastion.

The runtime directories still use the old name: `config/floyd-*.yaml`, `data/floyd.db`, `.iii/compose/floyd`, and the `dist/floyd-ui-*` build files. Git ignores these directories, so I did not change them. The engine will create a new, empty `data/bastion.db`, so the data in `floyd.db` will not be carried over. Delete these old files, or rename `floyd.db` to `bastion.db` if you want to keep that data.

I made no commit, because you did not ask for one.

# Extract Anthropic out of Supabase into its own service

## Context

Today every Claude call runs inside a Supabase Edge Function, and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
lives as a Supabase/Lovable secret. The goal is to make Supabase do **database and edge
functions only** — no third-party AI credentials, no direct vendor calls — by moving the
Anthropic integration into its own module that owns the key.

Phase 1 covers Anthropic. Phase 2 generalises the config pattern to the remaining
secrets, where "Lovable stays the default, an explicit env var overrides it and switches
transport."

### What's actually there now

Five raw `fetch("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages")` call sites (Deno, no SDK, no
streaming), reached by seven logical paths:

| Call site | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `_shared/claude.ts:28` | text + base64 doc, 3000 tok | only caller is `parse-benefit-letter` (writes no tables — cleanest) |
| `_shared/classify.ts:52` | forced tool use, up to 9 blocks | up to 8 attachments × 15 MB |
| `review-document/index.ts:94` | forced tool use, ~4 KB schema | up to 3 calls/doc (retry + FMLA pass) |
| `policy-ingestion/index.ts:73` | system **array**, 16000 tok | chunked, 3-concurrent, **prompt caching** |
| `historical-leave-extract/index.ts:113` | static system, 16000 tok | **fully synchronous — user waits** |

Each one is a single self-contained function (`askClaude`, `classify`, `readPart`, …)
whose only provider coupling is the URL and headers, so the per-site diff is genuinely
small. `CLAUDE_MODEL` is never hardcoded. `_shared/anthropic.ts` builds the headers, but
`policy-ingestion` and `historical-leave-extract` inline the same block instead of
importing it.

### Constraints that shape the design

- **No CI exists.** Edge functions are deployed by Lovable on commit; secrets are set in
  the Supabase/Lovable dashboard. There is no pipeline to hook into.
- **A precedent already exists.** `pay-periods/index.ts:3-9` proxies to an external Fly
  service with a static `X-API-Key`. We follow that shape.
- **Prompt caching must survive.** `policy-ingestion/index.ts:77` is the only
  `cache_control: ephemeral` user in the repo; breaking it is a real cost regression.
- **Payloads are large.** Worst case ~8 × 15 MB of base64 in one body.
- **Prompt-injection guards must be preserved verbatim** — `classify.ts:43` and
  `review-document/index.ts:112` both instruct the model to treat document text as
  content, not instructions. These are security-relevant; copy them exactly.

## Recommended approach

### Phase 1 — Anthropic

**1. New service at `server/` in this repo**

A thin, faithful passthrough — not semantic endpoints. `POST /v1/messages` mirrors
Anthropic's Messages API body exactly; the service injects `x-api-key`,
`anthropic-version`, the default model, retry and timeout. Edge functions keep building
their own prompts and parsing their own responses, so forced tool use, the system-block
array and `cache_control` all pass through untouched and the diff per call site is just
URL + headers.

- `POST /v1/messages` — auth, size cap, retry/backoff on 429/5xx, timeout, then proxy
- `GET /v1/health` — must prove the **service** is up, not just nginx (see below)

input.content:
# Bastion plan

Bastion is an agent-first development environment, in the spirit of
Antigravity, built on the iii engine. It is one native app: a Tauri 2 window
with a Leptos frontend and a Rust core. It has two surfaces. The **editor** is
where the owner reads and writes code. The **Agent Manager** is where the owner
starts agents, watches them work in parallel, and reviews what they produce.
Agents run on iii workers, against a local engine that the app starts. A remote
engine on the owner's own box comes later (§10). Written 2026-10-30, revised the
same day.

The full editor is the most expensive choice in this plan. It adds language
servers and one JavaScript exception (D1), and it is two phases on its own. The
owner chose it over a manager that opens files in another editor.

## 1. Goals

1. One native app on macOS and Linux runs Bastion against a local `iii` engine.
   No terminal is needed after install.
2. The owner edits code in Bastion: a file tree, tabs, syntax highlighting,
   search, diffs, and language-server diagnostics, completion and navigation.
3. The owner runs several agent tasks at once, each in its own worktree and
   sandbox VM, and sees each task's state in one view.
4. Every agent output a person must judge is an **artifact**: a task list, a
   plan, a diff, a test result, a screenshot, a recording or a walkthrough. A
   comment on an artifact goes back to the agent as its next instruction.
5. Work runs free-form (one task, one agent) or through a **pipeline**: wipp's
   phased factory, with a person's decision at each checkpoint.
6. An agent can drive a browser, and its screenshots and recordings are
   artifacts.
7. Nothing merges itself. A person decides every merge.
8. A task that needs the owner raises a native notification within 2 s.
9. No Bastion process serves HTTP. The engine listens on loopback only.

## 2. Non-goals

- Not a browser app, and no HTTP API.
- Not multi-user. One owner, on their own machine. No sign-in.
- Not a VS Code fork, and no VS Code extension host. The editor is Bastion's
  own, built on CodeMirror 6 (D1).
- Not a new agent runtime. Turns run on the stock `harness`, `llm-router` and
  `iii-sandbox` workers.
- Not hosted. wipp runs on Fly for a GitHub org. Bastion runs on the owner's
  machine.
- Not a remote client yet. The owner's box is §10.
- Not Windows. Sandbox VMs need Apple Silicon or Linux with `/dev/kvm`.

## 3. Fixed decisions

| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Rust for all Bastion code. The one planned exception is a vendored, prebuilt CodeMirror 6 bundle that the editor drives through `wasm-bindgen`. Any other JavaScript is named in §4 with its reason. | One language. No Rust editor component comes close to CodeMirror, and a vendored bundle needs no Node toolchain. |
| D2 | Tauri 2, the stable line. `cargo search` shows 3.0.0-alpha.5 on 2026-10-30, so 3 waits. | A native app with a Rust core. |
| D3 | The frontend is Leptos 0.8, client-side rendered to WASM and built by Trunk. | Rust pages in Tauri's webview. |
| D4 | One dark theme, purple as the main color (`--primary: #7c3aed`, `--primary-hover: #6d28d9`, `--link: #c4b5fd`). No light theme. Tailwind 4 runs as Trunk's standalone binary. | The owner's choice. No Node toolchain. |
| D5 | One Cargo workspace: the frontend crate at the root, the app in `src-tauri/`, shared code in `crates/`, Bastion workers in `workers/` (§4). | One build, one lockfile, one CI. |
| D6 | Every Bastion worker is a Rust binary on `iii-sdk` 0.25.0. Compose starts it through `scripts.run`. | The same engine, with no second runtime. |
| D7 | A stock registry worker comes first. Bastion writes a worker only for what no pinned worker does, and §5 records each choice. | Less code to own. The stack already pins `harness`, `iii-sandbox`, `worktree`, `ide`, `approval-gate`, `workflow`, `session-manager`, `github` and `storage`. |
| D8 | Bastion's records (tasks, artifacts, comments, decisions) live in the `database` worker as typed columns. Each row carries a `rev`, and a stale write is refused. | wipp lost a live job in the `state` worker on restart, and a last write once overrode a Stop. |
| D9 | The pages reach the engine only through typed Tauri commands. A command maps to one engine function or one core routine, and no command takes a function id. | One narrow surface, listed in one file. |
| D10 | Live updates are push. The core observes `bastion::*::changed` and emits a Tauri event `{kind, id, revision}`, and the page reads the resource again. | wipp polled. Push needs no timers and no stale views. |
| D11 | One owner, no sign-in. The actor on every record is `git config user.name`. | One person on one machine needs no accounts. |
| D12 | Local is the default and only mode for now. The engine address is a profile field, never a constant. | The remote box (§10) becomes a new profile kind, not a rewrite. |
| D13 | The app starts the stack with `iii compose --up -f worker-compose.yaml`, and attaches to a stack that already runs. On quit, the owner chooses whether it keeps running. | The owner's choice. No terminal. |
| D14 | Every agent turn runs in an `iii-sandbox` VM on its task's worktree. A credential never enters the VM. Pushes and PRs happen on the host. | wipp's lesson: a sprite that saw a credential is tainted. |
| D15 | Merge is a person's decision, or `hold` at the lowest. Every other checkpoint has a dial: `ask`, `hold` (default after 30 min) or `auto`. | wipp's oversight model. |
| D16 | A comment on an artifact goes to the agent verbatim, as its next brief. A fix loop stops after a set count, or sooner when a refusal repeats word for word. | wipp's bounded loops. Paraphrased feedback loses the point. |

## 4. The repository

```
Cargo.toml  index.html  Trunk.toml  styles.css
src/                  bastion-ui: the Leptos frontend (WASM)
  editor/             the editor surface
  manager/            the Agent Manager surface
  vendor/codemirror/  the prebuilt bundle (D1)
src-tauri/            bastion: Tauri, the Rust core
  src/engine.rs       the iii-sdk link
  src/commands/       one file per resource (D9)
  src/stack.rs        iii compose as a child process
  src/doctor.rs
crates/
  bastion-core/       shared types: task, artifact, pipeline, checkpoint
  bastion-spikes/     spikes and live checks, as examples
workers/
  bastion-tasks/      tasks, artifacts, comments, checkpoints
  bastion-lsp/        language servers, one per workspace and language
  bastion-browser/    a browser driven over CDP
worker-compose.yaml   the stack the app starts
PLAN.md  docs/
```

`cargo tauri dev` runs the app.

**JavaScript that may remain (D1):** `src/vendor/codemirror/`, built once from
CodeMirror 6 and checked in with its version and license. Nothing else is
planned.

## 5. Where each feature lives

**Put it in a worker when** it keeps state, runs while the app is closed, or a
turn or another worker needs it. The app on a laptop then reaches it on the box
later (§10).

**Put it in the app's core when** it is about this machine or this window: it
must run before the engine is up, it only shapes what the page shows, or it
talks to the OS.

| Feature | Home | Worker | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stack start, stop, attach, logs | app | — | A1 |
| Doctor | app: it runs before the engine | — | A1 |
| Profiles | app | — | A1 |
| Engine console: workers, functions, triggers, queues | app view over the engine | engine built-ins | A2 |
| File reads, writes, search, the fs jail | worker | `ide` (stock) | A3 |
| Language servers | worker | `bastion-lsp` | A4 |
| Worktrees and local land | worker | `worktree` (stock) | A5 |
| Agent turns | worker | `harness`, `llm-router`, `iii-sandbox` (stock) | A5 |
| Transcripts | worker | `session-manager` (stock) | A5 |
| Tasks, artifacts, comments, checkpoints | worker | `bastion-tasks` | A5 |
| Approvals | worker | `approval-gate` (stock) | A6 |
| Push, PRs, CI watch, merge | worker | `github` (stock) | A6 |
| Pipelines | worker | `workflow` (stock), if A7's spike passes | A7 |
| Browser | worker | `bastion-browser` | A8 |
| Notifications and tray | app | — | A9 |

`ade` is iii's own console, on `127.0.0.1:3114`. It stays in the stack until
A2's console covers what the owner uses in it, and then it leaves.

## 6. Concepts

- **Workspace:** a repository folder the owner opens. The editor and the
  Agent Manager share it.
- **Task:** one request to an agent in one workspace. It owns one worktree,
  one sandbox VM and one transcript. States: `queued`, `running`,
  `needs_you`, `blocked`, `landed`, `closed`, `failed`, `stopped`.
- **Artifact:** a typed output of a task: task list, plan, diff, test result,
  screenshot, recording, walkthrough. Bytes go to `storage`; the row goes to
  `database`.
- **Comment:** the owner's note on an artifact, or on one line of a diff. It
  becomes the task's next brief (D16).
- **Checkpoint:** a point where a person decides, with a dial (D15).
- **Pipeline:** a template of stages a task moves through. Free-form is the
  pipeline with one stage.

## 7. Phases

Each phase uses paired pacing and stops at its exit evidence, run live after
its last change. A phase that rests on an unproven engine feature starts with
a spike, and a failed spike stops the phase with its fallback named. Sizes: S,
M, L.

### A0 — Spikes (M)

**Goal:** prove that Rust on `iii-sdk` 0.25.0 and Tauri can do what the rest of
the plan assumes.

- **N1:** a Rust worker registers a function, triggers one, observes a
  `changed` function, and calls `database::query` and `database::transaction`.
- **N2:** it enqueues with `TriggerAction::Enqueue` on `bastion-steps`, and
  sends with `Void`.
- **N3:** it binds `harness::turn-completed` for one session, and a
  `harness::hook::pre-trigger` that rewrites `sandbox_id`.
- **N4:** it reads a `sandbox::fs::read` content channel.
- **N5:** compose starts a Rust binary through `scripts.run`, and restarts it.
- **N6:** a Tauri 2 window shows a Leptos page in the dark purple theme. An
  `invoke` round trip works, and the core emits an event the page receives.

# Bastion plan

Bastion is a native software factory on the iii engine, with an Agent Manager
in the spirit of Antigravity's. It is one app: a Tauri 2 window with a Leptos
frontend and a Rust core. The owner starts agent tasks, watches them work in
parallel, reviews what they produce, and decides what lands. Agents run on iii
workers, against a local engine that the app starts. A remote engine on the
owner's own box comes later (§10). Written 2026-10-30, revised the same day.

Bastion is not an editor. The owner keeps their own editor. The one view of
code inside Bastion is the diff a task proposes.

## 1. Goals

1. One native app on macOS and Linux runs Bastion against a local `iii` engine.
   No terminal is needed after install.
2. The owner runs several agent tasks at once, each in its own worktree and
   sandbox VM, and sees each task's state in one view.
3. Every agent output a person must judge is an **artifact**: a task list, a
   plan, a diff, a test result, a screenshot, a recording or a walkthrough. A
   comment on an artifact goes back to the agent as its next instruction.
4. Work runs free-form (one task, one agent) or through a **pipeline**: wipp's
   phased factory, with a person's decision at each checkpoint.
5. An agent can drive a browser, and its screenshots and recordings are
   artifacts.
6. Nothing merges itself. A person decides every merge.
7. A task that needs the owner raises a native notification within 2 s.
8. No Bastion process serves HTTP. The engine listens on loopback only.

## 2. Non-goals

- Not an editor or a file browser. The diff artifact is the only view of code.
  "Open in editor" hands a worktree path to the owner's own editor.
- Not a browser app, and no HTTP API.
- Not multi-user. One owner, on their own machine. No sign-in.
- Not a new agent runtime. Turns run on the stock `harness`, `llm-router` and
  `iii-sandbox` workers.
- Not hosted. wipp runs on Fly for a GitHub org. Bastion runs on the owner's
  machine.
- Not a remote client yet. The owner's box is §10.
- Not Windows. Sandbox VMs need Apple Silicon or Linux with `/dev/kvm`.

## 3. Fixed decisions

| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Rust for all Bastion code. TypeScript or JavaScript only where no Rust path exists, and each such file is named in §4 with its reason. | One language. |
| D2 | Tauri 2, the stable line. `cargo search` shows 3.0.0-alpha.5 on 2026-10-30, so 3 waits. | A native app with a Rust core. |
| D3 | The frontend is Leptos 0.8, client-side rendered to WASM and built by Trunk. | Rust pages in Tauri's webview. |
| D4 | One dark theme, purple as the main color (`--primary: #7c3aed`, `--primary-hover: #6d28d9`, `--link: #c4b5fd`). No light theme. Tailwind 4 runs as Trunk's standalone binary. | The owner's choice. No Node toolchain. |
| D5 | One Cargo workspace: the frontend crate at the root, the app in `src-tauri/`, shared code in `crates/`, Bastion workers in `workers/` (§4). | One build, one lockfile, one CI. |
| D6 | Every Bastion worker is a Rust binary on `iii-sdk` 0.25.0. Compose starts it through `scripts.run`. | The same engine, with no second runtime. |
| D7 | A stock registry worker comes first. Bastion writes a worker only for what no pinned worker does, and §5 records each choice. | Less code to own. The stack already pins `harness`, `iii-sandbox`, `worktree`, `approval-gate`, `workflow`, `session-manager`, `github` and `storage`. |
| D8 | Bastion's records (tasks, artifacts, comments, decisions) live in the `database` worker as typed columns. Each row carries a `rev`, and a stale write is refused. | wipp lost a live job in the `state` worker on restart, and a last write once overrode a Stop. |
| D9 | The pages reach the engine only through typed Tauri commands. A command maps to one engine function or one core routine, and no command takes a function id. | One narrow surface, listed in one file. |
| D10 | Live updates are push. The core observes `bastion::*::changed` and emits a Tauri event `{kind, id, revision}`, and the page reads the resource again. | wipp polled. Push needs no timers and no stale views. |
| D11 | One owner, no sign-in. The actor on every record is `git config user.name`. | One person on one machine needs no accounts. |
| D12 | Local is the default and only mode for now. The engine address is a profile field, never a constant. | The remote box (§10) becomes a new profile kind, not a rewrite. |
| D13 | The app starts the stack with `iii compose --up -f worker-compose.yaml`, and attaches to a stack that already runs. On quit, the owner chooses whether it keeps running. | The owner's choice. No terminal. |
| D14 | Every agent turn runs in an `iii-sandbox` VM on its task's worktree. A credential never enters the VM. Pushes and PRs happen on the host. | wipp's lesson: a sprite that saw a credential is tainted. |

src/                  bastion-ui: the Leptos frontend (WASM)

## 9. Lessons from wipp

wipp (`~/Code/wipp`) is the model for the pipeline. These lessons carry over.

| Lesson | Where it lands |
|---|---|
| The `state` worker lost a live job on restart. | D8: rows in `database`. |
| A last write overrode Stop. | D8: `rev` on every row. |
| A turn that never ended stalled its job forever. | A3: every turn has a time cap. |
| A credential in a VM taints the VM. | D14: pushes happen on the host. |
| Feedback paraphrased by the factory lost the point. | D16: comments go verbatim. |
| A fix loop with no bound ran until it was stopped. | D16: a count, and a stop on a repeated refusal. |
| The gate's own audit log stopped answering, and every call was refused. | A3: the audit path has a timeout test, and its failure shows in the console. |
| iii upgrades broke pins and config names. | A8: the app refuses a stack it does not know. |

## 10. Later: the owner's box

The app will reach a stack on a box the owner controls, after A8. Nothing here
starts until the owner asks.

- **Transport:** an SSH tunnel to the engine port on the box's loopback, with
  the owner's own SSH config and agent. The app stores no SSH key.
- **Profile:** a new `kind = "remote"`, with `ssh_host` and the far port (D12).
- **Spike first:** N1 passes through the tunnel.
- Features in workers need nothing new. The app's core features (Doctor, the
  stack) run on the box over SSH.
- Diffs come from `bastion-tasks` on the box, so review needs no file sync.
- The title bar names the profile.
- **Exit, live:** from the laptop, a task on the box lands. The tunnel is killed
  mid-task, the app reconnects, and the task finishes once.

## 11. Risks

| Risk | What settles it |
|---|---|
| N3 passed two of three runs, and the cause of the failure is unknown. | A0's exit needs three passes in a row. |
| `workflow` 0.1.9 is young. | A5's spike, with `bastion-steps` as the fallback. |
| CDP screencasts may be hard to turn into a playable recording. | A6's spike. The fallback is a frame sequence shown as a slideshow. |
| A large diff may be slow to render in the webview. | A4 renders one file at a time, and collapses files over a set size. |
| App checks have no driver on macOS. | Linux CI runs `tauri-driver`. |

## 12. Progress

| Phase | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A0 | in progress | N1, N2, N4, N5 pass (2026-10-30). N3 passed two of three runs. N6 is built in the app at the root, and its live run has not been recorded. |
| A1 to A8 | — | — |
| Later (§10) | on hold | — |

input.content:
# Bastion plan

Bastion is a native software factory on the iii engine. A request goes in, a
reviewed change comes out, and nothing merges itself. It is one app: a Tauri 2
window with a Leptos frontend and a Rust core. Agents run on iii workers,
against a local engine that the app starts. A remote engine on the owner's own
box comes later (§10). Written 2026-10-30, revised the same day.

The owner works at the level of the factory. The first view is the **floor**:
every job, the stage it is in, and the decisions waiting on the owner. Agents
and their transcripts sit one level down, for when a job needs a closer look.
Antigravity starts at the agent; Bastion starts at the job. wipp is the model
for the pipeline and its checkpoints.

Bastion is not an editor. The owner keeps their own editor. The one view of
code inside Bastion is the diff a job proposes.

## 1. Goals

1. One native app on macOS and Linux runs Bastion against a local `iii` engine.
   No terminal is needed after install.
2. The floor shows every job, its stage and its state, and the inbox shows
   every decision waiting on the owner. Both update by push.
3. A job moves through a **pipeline** of stages. Agents do the work in each
   stage, several jobs at once, each in its own worktree and sandbox VM.
4. Every stage leaves an **artifact** a person can judge: a plan, a test
   result, a diff, a screenshot, a recording or a briefing. A comment on an
   artifact goes back to the agent as its next instruction.
5. An agent can drive a browser, and its screenshots and recordings are
   artifacts.
6. Nothing merges itself. A person decides every merge.
7. A job that needs the owner raises a native notification within 2 s.
8. No Bastion process serves HTTP. The engine listens on loopback only.

## 2. Non-goals

- Not an editor or a file browser. The diff artifact is the only view of code.
  "Open in editor" hands a worktree path to the owner's own editor.
- Not an agent chat. The owner talks to a job through its artifacts and
  checkpoints, not through a prompt box per agent.
- Not a browser app, and no HTTP API.
- Not multi-user. One owner, on their own machine. No sign-in.
- Not a new agent runtime. Turns run on the stock `harness`, `llm-router` and
  `iii-sandbox` workers.
- Not hosted. wipp runs on Fly for a GitHub org. Bastion runs on the owner's
  machine.
- Not a remote client yet. The owner's box is §10.
- Not Windows. Sandbox VMs need Apple Silicon or Linux with `/dev/kvm`.

## 3. Fixed decisions

| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Rust for all Bastion code. TypeScript or JavaScript only where no Rust path exists, and each such file is named in §4 with its reason. | One language. |
| D2 | Tauri 2, the stable line. `cargo search` shows 3.0.0-alpha.5 on 2026-10-30, so 3 waits. | A native app with a Rust core. |
| D3 | The frontend is Leptos 0.8, client-side rendered to WASM and built by Trunk. | Rust pages in Tauri's webview. |
| D4 | One dark theme, purple as the main color (`--primary: #7c3aed`, `--primary-hover: #6d28d9`, `--link: #c4b5fd`). No light theme. Tailwind 4 runs as Trunk's standalone binary. | The owner's choice. No Node toolchain. |
| D5 | One Cargo workspace: the frontend crate at the root, the app in `src-tauri/`, shared code in `crates/`, Bastion workers in `workers/` (§4). | One build, one lockfile, one CI. |
| D6 | Every Bastion worker is a Rust binary on `iii-sdk` 0.25.0. Compose starts it through `scripts.run`. | The same engine, with no second runtime. |
| D7 | A stock registry worker comes first. Bastion writes a worker only for what no pinned worker does, and §5 records each choice. | Less code to own. The stack already pins `harness`, `iii-sandbox`, `worktree`, `approval-gate`, `workflow`, `session-manager`, `github` and `storage`. |
| D8 | Bastion's records (jobs, stages, artifacts, comments, decisions) live in the `database` worker as typed columns. Each row carries a `rev`, and a stale write is refused. | wipp lost a live job in the `state` worker on restart, and a last write once overrode a Stop. |
| D9 | The pages reach the engine only through typed Tauri commands. A command maps to one engine function or one core routine, and no command takes a function id. | One narrow surface, listed in one file. |
| D10 | Live updates are push. The core observes `bastion::*::changed` and emits a Tauri event `{kind, id, revision}`, and the page reads the resource again. | wipp polled. Push needs no timers and no stale views. |
| D11 | One owner, no sign-in. The actor on every record is `git config user.name`. | One person on one machine needs no accounts. |
| D12 | Local is the default and only mode for now. The engine address is a profile field, never a constant. | The remote box (§10) becomes a new profile kind, not a rewrite. |
| D13 | The app starts the stack with `iii compose --up -f worker-compose.yaml`, and attaches to a stack that already runs. On quit, the owner chooses whether it keeps running. | The owner's choice. No terminal. |
| D14 | Every agent turn runs in an `iii-sandbox` VM on its job's worktree. A credential never enters the VM. Pushes and PRs happen on the host. | wipp's lesson: a sprite that saw a credential is tainted. |
| D15 | Merge is a person's decision, or `hold` at the lowest. Every other checkpoint has a dial: `ask`, `hold` (default after 30 min) or `auto`. | wipp's oversight model. |
| D16 | A comment on an artifact goes to the agent verbatim, as its next brief. A fix loop stops after a set count, or sooner when a refusal repeats word for word. | wipp's bounded loops. Paraphrased feedback loses the point. |
| D17 | Every job runs a pipeline. The smallest pipeline is plan, approve, build, review, land, and it is the default until A5 adds the rest. | The factory is the unit. A free-form task is a short pipeline, not a second mode. |

## 4. The repository

```
Cargo.toml  index.html  Trunk.toml  styles.css
src/                  bastion-ui: the Leptos frontend (WASM)
src-tauri/            bastion: Tauri, the Rust core
  src/engine.rs       the iii-sdk link
  src/commands/       one file per resource (D9)
  src/stack.rs        iii compose as a child process
  src/doctor.rs
crates/
  bastion-core/       shared types: job, stage, artifact, pipeline, checkpoint
  bastion-spikes/     spikes and live checks, as examples
workers/
  bastion-factory/    jobs, stages, artifacts, comments, checkpoints
  bastion-browser/    a browser driven over CDP
worker-compose.yaml   the stack the app starts
PLAN.md  docs/
```

`cargo tauri dev` runs the app.

**JavaScript that may remain (D1):** none is planned.

## 5. Where each feature lives

**Put it in a worker when** it keeps state, runs while the app is closed, or a
turn or another worker needs it. The app on a laptop then reaches it on the box
later (§10).

**Put it in the app's core when** it is about this machine or this window: it
must run before the engine is up, it only shapes what the page shows, or it
talks to the OS.

| Feature | Home | Worker | Phase |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stack start, stop, attach, logs | app | — | A1 |
| Doctor | app: it runs before the engine | — | A1 |
| Profiles | app | — | A1 |
| Engine console: workers, functions, triggers, queues | app view over the engine | engine built-ins | A2 |
| Jobs, stages, artifacts, comments, checkpoints | worker | `bastion-factory` | A3 |
| Running a pipeline | worker | `workflow` (stock), if A3's spike passes | A3 |
| Worktrees and local land | worker | `worktree` (stock) | A3 |
| Agent turns | worker | `harness`, `llm-router`, `iii-sandbox` (stock) | A3 |
| Transcripts | worker | `session-manager` (stock) | A3 |
| Diffs | worker: computed in the job's worktree | `bastion-factory` | A4 |
| Approvals | worker | `approval-gate` (stock) | A4 |
| Push, PRs, CI watch, merge | worker | `github` (stock) | A4 |
| Browser | worker | `bastion-browser` | A6 |
| Notifications and tray | app | — | A7 |

`ade` is iii's own console, on `127.0.0.1:3114`. It stays in the stack until
A2's console covers what the owner uses in it, and then it leaves.

## 6. Concepts

From the top down:

- **Floor:** every job in flight, grouped by stage, with its state.
- **Inbox:** every checkpoint waiting on the owner, oldest first.
- **Workspace:** a repository the owner registers with Bastion.
- **Job:** one request against one workspace. It owns one worktree, one
  sandbox VM and one pipeline run. States: `queued`, `running`, `needs_you`,
  `blocked`, `landed`, `closed`, `failed`, `stopped`.
- **Pipeline:** the stages a job moves through. It is data, so a job can run a
  short one or the full one.
- **Stage:** one step of a pipeline. An agent stage runs one or more turns; a
  person stage is a checkpoint.
- **Checkpoint:** a point where a person decides, with a dial (D15).
- **Artifact:** a typed output of a stage: plan, test result, diff,
  screenshot, recording, briefing. Bytes go to `storage`; the row goes to
  `database`.
- **Comment:** the owner's note on an artifact, or on one line of a diff. It
  becomes the stage's next brief (D16).
- **Turn:** one agent run inside a stage, with its transcript. The lowest
  level the app shows.

## 7. Phases

Each phase uses paired pacing and stops at its exit evidence, run live after
its last change. A phase that rests on an unproven engine feature starts with
a spike, and a failed spike stops the phase with its fallback named. Sizes: S,
M, L.

### A0 — Spikes (M)

**Goal:** prove that Rust on `iii-sdk` 0.25.0 and Tauri can do what the rest of
the plan assumes.

- **N1:** a Rust worker registers a function, triggers one, observes a
  `changed` function, and calls `database::query` and `database::transaction`.
- **N2:** it enqueues with `TriggerAction::Enqueue` on `bastion-steps`, and
  sends with `Void`.
- **N3:** it binds `harness::turn-completed` for one session, and a
  `harness::hook::pre-trigger` that rewrites `sandbox_id`.
- **N4:** it reads a `sandbox::fs::read` content channel.
- **N5:** compose starts a Rust binary through `scripts.run`, and restarts it.
- **N6:** a Tauri 2 window shows a Leptos page in the dark purple theme. An
  `invoke` round trip works, and the core emits an event the page receives.

**Exit:** N1 to N6 pass, and N3 passes three runs in a row. Each result goes in
`docs/levels.md` with the version of each part.

### A1 — The shell and the stack (M)

**Goal:** the app starts, checks, watches and stops the stack.

- The shell: a sidebar with Floor, Inbox, Engine and Settings, a skip link,
  and the dark theme.
- The engine link, with reconnect and backoff. The `this machine` profile, in
  TOML in the OS config directory, with no secret (D12).
- Doctor: `iii` and its version, the pins in `worker-compose.yaml`, provider
  keys, `gh` login, and sandbox support. Each failed check names its fix.
- The stack routine: Start runs Doctor and stops on a failed required check,
  then runs `iii compose --up`. Stop runs `iii kill --compose`. A stack that
  already runs is attached, not started twice. On quit, the owner chooses.
- CI on macOS and Linux: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`,
  `cargo test`.
- Replace the template `README.md`.

**Exit, live:** from a stopped machine, the app starts the stack and shows the
link as up. Doctor names a missing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with its fix. After a
quit with the stack kept running, the next start attaches. CI passes.

### A2 — The engine console (S)

**Goal:** the owner sees the engine without `ade`.

- Workers with their versions and state, from `compose::status`.
- Functions and triggers, from `engine::functions::list`.
- Queues and their depth.
- Live logs for one worker, from `compose::logs`.

**Exit, live:** stop one container from the console, see its state change by
push, start it again, and read its logs. Remove `ade` from the stack if the
owner no longer needs it.

### A3 — The floor (L)

**Goal:** a request becomes a job that runs the short pipeline (D17), and the
owner watches every job from the floor.

- **Spike first:** the stock `workflow` worker (0.1.9) runs a two-stage
  template with a person's checkpoint between them, and the run survives an
  engine restart. If it fails, `bastion-factory` runs stages from
  `bastion-steps` instead, as wipp does.
- `bastion-factory`: jobs, stages, artifacts, comments and checkpoints, as rows
  in `database` (D8), with `bastion::factory::changed` for push (D10).
- Register a workspace: a local repository path and its default branch.
- New request: a workspace and the request text. The job gets a worktree from
  `worktree` and a VM from `iii-sandbox`.
- Agent stages run turns on `harness`, with the model from `llm-router`. The
  workspace's charter (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`) goes into every turn. Every
  turn has a time cap.
- The floor: every job by stage, with its state and age. Up to
  `max_concurrent_sandboxes` (8) jobs run at once, and the rest queue.
- The inbox: each checkpoint with its artifact and its actions.
- The job view: the stage timeline, each stage's artifacts, and Stop. A turn's
  transcript from `session-manager` opens from its stage.
- An agent can stop with a question. The job goes to `needs_you`, and the
  answer starts the next turn.

**Exit, live:** submit three requests in two workspaces. Each job reaches the
approve checkpoint with a plan artifact, and the inbox shows three items. A
comment on one plan changes the next plan. Stop one job, and its VM is gone.
Restart the stack, and the two other jobs carry on from where they were.

### A4 — Review and landing (M)

**Goal:** a job's work lands only after a person decides.

- The diff artifact: `bastion-factory` computes it in the job's worktree
  against its base. The page renders it per file, unified or side by side,
  with syntax colors, and shows only the changed files.
- Comments on a diff line, sent verbatim (D16).
- The checkpoint dial (D15), per checkpoint, with merge never below `hold`.
- Land locally with `worktree::land`, or push and open a PR through `github`.
  Watch CI, and a failure starts a bounded fix turn (D16).
- Merge after the owner's decision.
- "Open in editor" passes the worktree path to the owner's editor.

**Exit, live:** a job's diff gets a line comment, and the next diff answers it.
The job is approved and lands locally. Another opens a PR, a failing CI run is
fixed by the agent, and the owner merges it.

### A5 — The full pipeline (L)

**Goal:** a job can run wipp's whole factory.

- The full pipeline, after wipp: scope, clarify, plan, approve; acceptance
  tests first, and the baseline must fail; one build turn per plan item, tests
  first; checks; refactor; review; ship; CI fix; merge; a briefing of what
  changed and why.
- Split a job into parts that depend on each other. The floor shows parts
  under their job.
- Read-only stages get a read-only grant. A changed tree in one is reverted.
- The owner picks a pipeline per request, and sets the dial per checkpoint.

**Exit, live:** a request in this repository runs the full pipeline to a
merged change. Each stage leaves an artifact, the baseline tests fail before
the build and pass after it, and each checkpoint obeys its dial.

### A6 — The browser agent (M)

**Goal:** an agent checks its work in a real browser, and the owner sees what
it saw.

- **Spike first:** `bastion-browser` drives Chrome over CDP with
  `chromiumoxide`. A screenshot and a screencast reach `storage`.
- Browser tools for turns: open, click, type, read the page, screenshot, and
  record.
- Screenshots and recordings are artifacts in the stage that made them.
- A pipeline can require a browser check before review.

**Exit, live:** a job changes a page in a test app, and its browser check
records the page. The owner comments on the screenshot, and the next turn
fixes what the comment names.

### A7 — Notifications and tray (M)

**Goal:** the owner learns that a job needs them without watching the window.

- Notify on `needs_you`, `blocked`, `failed` and `landed`. A click opens the
  inbox item or the job.
- The tray shows the inbox count and the stack state, with start and stop.
- After a reconnect, the core reads every active job again.
- A setting turns each kind of notification off.

**Exit, live:** a checkpoint raises a notification within 2 s. A click opens
it, the approval moves the job on, and the tray count goes from 1 to 0.

### A8 — Packaging and updates (M)

**Goal:** the app installs and updates itself on another machine.

- A signed and notarized macOS build for Apple Silicon, and an AppImage and a
  `.deb` for Linux.
- `tauri-plugin-updater` with a signed manifest from GitHub releases.
- The app checks each Bastion worker's version, and refuses a stack it does not
  know, with the fix.
- A release workflow in CI, from a tag.

**Exit, live:** on a clean Mac, install from the release and start the stack
from the app. Publish a newer release, and the app updates itself.

## 8. Verification rules

- Each exit runs live, after the phase's last change.
- Rust passes `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
  `cargo test` across the workspace.
- App checks run through `tauri-driver` in Linux CI. It has no macOS support,
  so macOS gets the Rust tests and a manual smoke test.
- Each changed file passes the CodeScene review and the pre-commit safeguard.
- A live check that spends money says so first, with its rough cost.

## 9. Lessons from wipp

wipp (`~/Code/wipp`) is the model for the pipeline. These lessons carry over.

| Lesson | Where it lands |
|---|---|
| The `state` worker lost a live job on restart. | D8: rows in `database`. |
| A last write overrode Stop. | D8: `rev` on every row. |
| A turn that never ended stalled its job forever. | A3: every turn has a time cap. |
| A credential in a VM taints the VM. | D14: pushes happen on the host. |
| Feedback paraphrased by the factory lost the point. | D16: comments go verbatim. |
| A fix loop with no bound ran until it was stopped. | D16: a count, and a stop on a repeated refusal. |
| The gate's own audit log stopped answering, and every call was refused. | A3: the audit path has a timeout test, and its failure shows in the console. |
| iii upgrades broke pins and config names. | A8: the app refuses a stack it does not know. |

## 10. Later: the owner's box

The app will reach a stack on a box the owner controls, after A8. Nothing here
starts until the owner asks.

- **Transport:** an SSH tunnel to the engine port on the box's loopback, with
  the owner's own SSH config and agent. The app stores no SSH key.
- **Profile:** a new `kind = "remote"`, with `ssh_host` and the far port (D12).
- **Spike first:** N1 passes through the tunnel.
- Features in workers need nothing new. The app's core features (Doctor, the
  stack) run on the box over SSH.
- Diffs come from `bastion-factory` on the box, so review needs no file sync.
- The title bar names the profile.
- **Exit, live:** from the laptop, a job on the box lands. The tunnel is killed
  mid-job, the app reconnects, and the job finishes once.

## 11. Risks

| Risk | What settles it |
|---|---|
| N3 passed two of three runs, and the cause of the failure is unknown. | A0's exit needs three passes in a row. |
| `workflow` 0.1.9 is young. | A3's spike, with `bastion-steps` as the fallback. |
| CDP screencasts may be hard to turn into a playable recording. | A6's spike. The fallback is a frame sequence shown as a slideshow. |
| A large diff may be slow to render in the webview. | A4 renders one file at a time, and collapses files over a set size. |
| App checks have no driver on macOS. | Linux CI runs `tauri-driver`. |

## 12. Progress

| Phase | State | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| A0 | in progress | N1, N2, N4, N5 pass (2026-10-30). N3 passed two of three runs. N6 is built in the app at the root, and its live run has not been recorded. |
| A1 to A8 | — | — |
| Later (§10) | on hold | — |

### 6.1 Three layers

| Layer | Where | Knows | Does not know |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core** | `crates/bastion-core` | The factory's rules: which stage comes next, when a checkpoint waits, what the dial does, when a fix loop stops, what a brief says. | iii, Tauri, Leptos, the clock, the disk. |
| **Engine adapter** | `src-tauri/src/engine/` | How to run each effect on iii, and how to turn each engine event into a core event. It persists every new state with its `rev` (D8). | Any factory rule. |
| **View** | `src/` | How to draw a resource, and which typed command to call (D9). | iii and the factory's rules. |

One loop joins them. An event arrives: the owner's decision through a command,
or an engine event such as a turn that completed. The adapter loads the job,
calls the core, writes the new state, runs the effects the core returned, and
emits the change to the page (D10). An effect is data, such as "start a turn
with this brief" or "open a PR". The core never waits on one.

On start, the adapter reads every active job and resumes it. The core also
lives in the app's Tauri commands' read paths, so the view never computes a
rule itself, for example whether a button is enabled.

### 6.2 Seams

Each seam is named, has one owner, and has a fake that tests use. Crate
dependencies enforce the seams, so code that crosses one does not compile
(D19).

| Seam | Shape | Owner | Fake in tests |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Event in, decision out** | `bastion_core::step(state, event) -> (state, Vec<Effect>)`. `Event` and `Effect` are enums. The time comes in on the event. | `bastion-core` | None needed: the core is pure, so tests call `step` directly. |
| **Engine** | A trait in the adapter: `call`, `observe`, `register`. The only code that imports `iii-sdk`. | `src-tauri/src/engine/` | An in-memory engine that records calls and replays events. |
| **Store** | A trait in the adapter: load a job, save a job with its `rev`, list active jobs. Backed by `database` through the Engine seam. | `src-tauri/src/engine/` | An in-memory store that refuses a stale `rev`. |
| **Commands** | The typed Tauri commands and their request and response types, in `crates/bastion-protocol`. The view and the app both depend on it. | `bastion-protocol` | The view's tests use canned responses. |

Allowed dependencies:

```
bastion-ui (view)  ──>  bastion-protocol
bastion (app)      ──>  bastion-protocol, bastion-core, iii-sdk, tauri
bastion-core       ──>  serde only
bastion-protocol   ──>  serde only
```

`bastion-core` and `bastion-protocol` never depend on each other's internals.
The app maps between them, so the core's types can change without changing
the page.

I updated `PLAN.md` for both requests. Nothing is committed yet.

**All factory logic in the app (D18):** `crates/bastion-core` is a pure crate with one function: `step(state, event) -> (state, Vec<Effect>)`. It holds the factory rules: jobs, pipelines, checkpoints, the dial, fix loops, and briefs. It does no I/O and has no `async`, and it depends only on `serde`. The time arrives as part of each event, so tests call `step` directly.

**Three layers (§6.1):**
- **Core:** `bastion-core`, as above.
- **Engine adapter:** `src-tauri/src/engine/` is the only code that imports `iii-sdk`. It runs one loop: load the job, call `step`, save with its `rev`, run the effects, and emit the change to the page.
- **View:** `src/` only draws pages and calls typed commands.

**Clean seams (§6.2, D19):** there are four named seams: Event/Effect, Engine, Store, and Commands. The Engine and Store seams are traits with in-memory fakes. Commands live in a new `crates/bastion-protocol`, which the view and the app share. The allowed dependencies are written in the plan. A CI check fails if `bastion-core` or `bastion-protocol` gains a dependency other than `serde`, or if `iii-sdk` appears outside `engine/`.

**Changes that follow from this:**
- The `bastion-factory` worker is gone, and the plan no longer uses the `workflow` worker or the `bastion-steps` queue.
- N2 is dropped, because the factory needs no queue.
- A1 now builds the seams first, and moves today's `iii-sdk` code behind the Engine trait.
- **Cost:** jobs advance only while the app runs. To limit that, the adapter resumes every active job on start, and A7 keeps the app running in the tray. If that is too limiting, a second adapter can host the same core in a worker, with no change to the core.

1	# Bastion plan
2	
3	Bastion is a native software factory on the iii engine. A request goes in, a
4	reviewed change comes out, and nothing merges itself. It is one app: a Tauri 2
5	window with a Leptos frontend and a Rust core. Agents run on iii workers,
6	against a local engine that the app starts. A remote engine on the owner's own
7	box comes later (§10). Written 2026-10-30, revised the same day.
8	
9	The owner works at the level of the factory. The first view is the **floor**:
10	every job, the stage it is in, and the decisions waiting on the owner. Agents
11	and their transcripts sit one level down, for when a job needs a closer look.
12	Antigravity starts at the agent; Bastion starts at the job. wipp is the model
13	for the pipeline and its checkpoints.
14	
15	Bastion is not an editor. The owner keeps their own editor. The one view of
16	code inside Bastion is the diff a job proposes.
17	
18	## 1. Goals
19	
20	1. One native app on macOS and Linux runs Bastion against a local `iii` engine.
21	   No terminal is needed after install.
22	2. The floor shows every job, its stage and its state, and the inbox shows
23	   every decision waiting on the owner. Both update by push.
24	3. A job moves through a **pipeline** of stages. Agents do the work in each
25	   stage, several jobs at once, each in its own worktree and sandbox VM.
26	4. Every stage leaves an **artifact** a person can judge: a plan, a test
27	   result, a diff, a screenshot, a recording or a briefing. A comment on an
28	   artifact goes back to the agent as its next instruction.
29	5. An agent can drive a browser, and its screenshots and recordings are
30	   artifacts.
31	6. Nothing merges itself. A person decides every merge.
32	7. A job that needs the owner raises a native notification within 2 s.
33	8. No Bastion process serves HTTP. The engine listens on loopback only.
34	
35	## 2. Non-goals
36	
37	- Not an editor or a file browser. The diff artifact is the only view of code.
38	  "Open in editor" hands a worktree path to the owner's own editor.
39	- Not an agent chat. The owner talks to a job through its artifacts and

# The checks every commit passes (PLAN.md §8, D19). The toolchain comes from
# rust-toolchain.toml.
name: ci

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  check:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [macos-latest, ubuntu-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Tauri's Linux libraries
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev librsvg2-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev patchelf

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      - name: Format
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

      - name: Seams
        run: scripts/check-seams.sh

      - name: Clippy, app and spikes
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --exclude bastion-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Clippy, view
        run: cargo clippy -p bastion-ui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings

      - name: Test
        run: cargo test --workspace --exclude bastion-ui

# Bastion

Bastion is a software factory that runs on your own machine. A request goes in,
agents work it through a pipeline of stages, and a reviewed change comes out.
Nothing merges itself. It's a native app (Tauri 2, Leptos, Rust) on the
[iii](https://iii.dev) engine, and it's early: the app shell, Doctor and the
stack controls work, and the factory itself starts in phase A3 of
[PLAN.md](PLAN.md).

```sh
cargo tauri dev
```

That opens the app. Go to **Engine**, press **Start**, and Bastion runs Doctor,
then brings up the stack in `worker-compose.yaml`. If the stack already runs,
the app attaches to it instead of starting a second one.

## What it is not

Not an editor: the only code you see in Bastion is the diff a job proposes. Not
a web app, and it serves no HTTP. Not multi-user: one owner, no sign-in. Not
Windows, because sandbox VMs need Apple Silicon or Linux with `/dev/kvm`.

## What you need

- Rust, from `rust-toolchain.toml` (rustup picks it up), and the
  `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target.
- `cargo install tauri-cli trunk`.
- `iii` 0.25.0 on your `PATH`.
- A model provider key, such as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`, in the
  environment you start Bastion from. The stack inherits it.
- `gh`, signed in, for pushes and pull requests. Landing locally works
  without it.

If something is missing, Doctor on the Engine page names it and says how to
fix it. A failed required check stops the start.

## How it fits together

| Part | Where | Does |
|---|---|---|
| View | `src/` | Draws the pages. Calls typed commands only. |
| Protocol | `crates/bastion-protocol` | The commands and events between the view and the app. |
| App | `src-tauri/` | Profiles, Doctor, the stack, and the engine adapter. |
| Engine adapter | `src-tauri/src/engine/` | The only code that imports `iii-sdk`. |
| Spikes | `crates/bastion-spikes` | The A0 checks, results in `docs/levels.md`. |

Each seam has a fake for tests, and `scripts/check-seams.sh` fails the build
when code crosses one (PLAN.md §6.2).

Your profile lives in `profiles.toml` in the OS config directory
(`~/Library/Application Support/dev.tacoda.bastion/` on macOS). It holds the
engine address and the checkout, and never a secret.

## Checks

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
scripts/check-seams.sh
cargo clippy --workspace --exclude bastion-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo clippy -p bastion-ui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --exclude bastion-ui
```

CI runs the same on macOS and Linux. Two live checks need a running stack:
`cargo test -p bastion -- --ignored --nocapture`.

## Next

[PLAN.md](PLAN.md) has the phases, A0 to A11, and the map to wipp's features.
Start with §6 if you want to change code: it says which layer owns what.

**A1 exit, run in the window this time:** from a stopped machine, Start ran Doctor and brought up all 24 containers. The link showed "Up, 378 functions" by push. I don't have a cost estimate for that yet; for scale, each N3 turn in A0 cost about $0.01. Errors carry stable `W###` codes; the ones worth branching on are `W210`
(already claimed), `W220` (dirty), `W221` (unmerged work), `W222` (files
held open by running processes), `W401` (land already queued), `W402`
(unresolved rebase from a previous land), and the land-block reasons
carried on events (`W410` conflict, `W411` tests, `W412` target kept
moving, `W413` target checked out dirty). `W5xx` means configuration
denied the operation, not that it failed: `W500` gate off, `W501` force
disabled, `W502` land target not in `gates.land_targets`, `W503`
repository not in `gates.repos`, `W504` per-repo worktree budget hit. The
message names the exact key; do not retry, surface that key to the
operator (or drop the force flag) instead.

## Reactive triggers

Register a `worktree::*` trigger when a different worker should react to
lifecycle changes without polling `worktree::list` — announce lands in
chat, start a follow-up agent when a sibling's branch merges, or alert on
blocked lands.

Reach for it when:

- A land's outcome should drive the next step (`worktree::landed`,
  `worktree::land-blocked` with `reason` and `conflict_files`).
- Ownership changes matter to an orchestrator (`worktree::claimed`,
  `worktree::released`).
- Cleanup should cascade (`worktree::removed`).

The caller of `worktree::land` gets only `{ job_id, queued }` back; the
outcome arrives on these triggers, so a landing workflow should always bind
one instead of polling.

### How to bind

1. Register a handler: `registerFunction('notify::on-land', handler)`.
2. Register the trigger:

```typescript
iii.registerTrigger({
  type: 'worktree::landed',
  function_id: 'notify::on-land',
  config: {
    // optional equality filters:
    // repo_path, worktree_id, session_id
  },
})
```

All six types accept the same three optional filters; unknown config keys
are rejected at registration. For event payload shapes, call
`get function info` on the trigger type.

**What A3 built:**
- **`bastion-core`:** the short pipeline (plan, approve, build, review, land) as a pure `step()`. It also holds the briefs, the `INTERRUPT:` question marker, the retry limit, and which actions the owner may take.

- **The factory loop:**
  - Admits up to 8 jobs at once and provisions each with a worktree and a VM.
  - Runs `harness` turns with the charter included and a 60-minute cap.
  - Records each stage's artifact.
  - Lands through `worktree::land`, then tears down.
  - Resumes jobs after a restart.
  - A test on the fakes drives a job from request to landed.

- Plan artifacts were cut off and showed literal `\n`, because `harness::status` truncates its result. The report now comes from the turn's last message in the session.

1	# Bastion plan
2	
3	Bastion is a native software factory on the iii engine. A request goes in, a
4	reviewed change comes out, and nothing merges itself. It is one app: a Tauri 2
5	window with a Leptos frontend and a Rust core. Agents run on iii workers,
6	against a local engine that the app starts. A remote engine on the owner's own
7	box comes later (§10). Written 2026-10-30, revised the same day.
8	
9	The **job** is the main idea: one request, like a ticket. The app reads like
10	GitHub Actions and like wipp's Jobs page. The first view lists every job, with
11	the ones waiting on the owner first. A job's page shows its pipeline as steps,
12	each with its state, its artifacts and its agent turns, and a panel at the top
13	when the job needs the owner. Antigravity starts at the agent; Bastion starts
14	at the job.
15	
16	Bastion reaches feature parity with wipp (`~/Code/wipp`, as of commit
17	`f7c7e02`): every feature wipp has, except the ones tied to hosting and to
18	more than one user (§7.1). Parity is at the level of features, not code: wipp
19	runs Claude Code in sprites.dev VMs, and Bastion runs `harness` turns in
20	`iii-sandbox` VMs.
21	
22	Bastion is not an editor. The owner keeps their own editor. The one view of
23	code inside Bastion is the diff a job proposes.
24	
25	## 1. Goals
26	
27	1. One native app on macOS and Linux runs Bastion against a local `iii` engine.
28	   No terminal is needed after install.
29	2. The Jobs page lists every job with its state and stage, the ones waiting
30	   on the owner first. The job page shows each step of its pipeline, as a run
31	   of GitHub Actions does. Both update by push.
32	3. A job moves through a **pipeline** of stages. Agents do the work in each
33	   stage, several jobs at once, each in its own worktree and sandbox VM.
34	4. Every stage leaves an **artifact** a person can judge: a plan, a test
35	   result, a diff, a screenshot, a recording or a briefing. A comment on an
36	   artifact goes back to the agent as its next instruction.
37	5. An agent can drive a browser, and its screenshots and recordings are
38	   artifacts.
39	6. Nothing merges itself. A person decides every merge.
40	7. A job that needs the owner raises a native notification within 2 s.
41	8. No Bastion process serves HTTP. The engine listens on loopback only.
42	9. Feature parity with wipp, with the exceptions §7.1 names.
43	
44	## 2. Non-goals
45	
46	- Not an editor or a file browser. The diff artifact is the only view of code.
47	  "Open in editor" hands a worktree path to the owner's own editor.
48	- Not an agent chat. The owner talks to a job through its artifacts and
49	  checkpoints, not through a prompt box per agent.
50	- Not a browser app, and no HTTP API.
51	- Not multi-user. One owner, on their own machine. No sign-in. This drops
52	  wipp's accounts, GitHub sign-in, org check and roles (§7.1).
53	- Not a new agent runtime. Turns run on the stock `harness`, `llm-router` and
54	  `iii-sandbox` workers.
55	- Not hosted. wipp runs on Fly for a GitHub org, behind Caddy. Bastion runs
56	  on the owner's machine, so the Fly deploy is not ported (§7.1).
57	- Not a remote client yet. The owner's box is §10.
58	- Not Windows. Sandbox VMs need Apple Silicon or Linux with `/dev/kvm`.

- **The plan is rewritten around your two points** (`c963b33`):
  - **Definitions:** charter (a project's own rules, or none), harness, and factory (Bastion is both).

  - **Goals and decisions:** goals 10–12, plus decisions D20 (rules as hooks), D21 (a tamper-evident hash-chain audit), D22 (A/B evals of harness configurations), and D23 (forge, tracker, CI, providers, and notifications as adapters you choose in Settings).
